question: Does SS OPS 1 conserve its reciprocal event ledger and respect causal rescheduling?
source_equations: docs/research/gross-test-02.md exact gate derivation and locked apparatus

method.action: H=kappa d-dagger P d + lambda N^2/2; d=z1-z2, P=ww-dagger, N=|z1|^2+|z2|^2; canonical complex Hamiltonian flow, no frozen memory in primary model.
method.units: All states, couplings and gate parameter s dimensionless. A gate spans s=0 to 1; s is not proper time.
method.domain: 12 directed events; 8 complex wave wires, 4 unit memory wires; explicit ordered reuse, identity physical transport. Four preparations at lambda=0 and 0.1, kappa=pi/2.
method.boundaries: Finite acyclic incidence, including a disconnected branch. No spatial mesh, boundary condition or continuum limit. Complete-cut charge accounts for every wire; event H is not asserted to be circuit energy.
method.initial_data: PCG64 runtime initialization stream from root 2026092502; normalized independent complex normal directions; wave norms uniform [0.35,0.85], memories unit norm; independent U(2) event frames.
method.solver: DOP853 rtol=2e-12 atol=2e-14 max_step=0.125, repeated at half both tolerances. Nine saved samples per gate. Exact constant-S solution is an independent control, not the numerical solver.
method.tolerances: Residuals <1e-9. Controls >1e-4 in every preparation. Complete real input Jacobian on preparation 0 for both lambdas; memory tangent directions preserve unit norm; central steps 1e-5 and 5e-6, agreement <1e-6.

hypotheses.prediction: Conservation and permissible schedules pass; no outside-ancestor response; independent frames agree; physical interventions are detected.
Missing backreaction, forbidden causal response or dependence on arbitrary event scheduling exceeds the frozen tolerances.

controls.purpose: Discriminate integration error from event-law failure
controls.method: Compare all saved circuit trajectories to closed constant-S solution; halve both numerical tolerances.
Compare two topological schedules and independent U(2) event frames with transformed wire transports; full central-difference input directions at two steps.

controls.purpose: Expose noncommutativity and missing reciprocal response
controls.method: Reverse two otherwise disjoint wave-pair events sharing one memory; separately freeze driven memory and compare with its exact external-memory solution.
